paper_sections.title: Neural representations of relevant and irrelevant features in perceptual decision making.
Main effects of task and stimulus type
Attention and accumulation in the frontal and parietal lobes

description.value: The study examined how selective attention to motion versus color modulates BOLD responses and neural representations of attended and ignored features during perceptual decision making.

design.value: Five highly trained human subjects performed a fully crossed motion coherence and color proportion discrimination task during six functional MRI task sessions, with separate motion and color localizer tasks and independent training-session data used for ROI generation.

description.value: Subjects identified the direction of motion or predominant color as quickly and accurately as possible.
Response time for the motion and color discrimination decisions.

source_definition.value: The proportion of dots moving coherently in a common direction, varied across six levels.
The proportion of dots assigned to the selected color, varied across six levels.
The attended feature was either motion or color, with the other feature ignored.

description.value: Five subjects, ages 26–38; two males. All subjects had normal neuroanatomy, were right-handed, and had normal or corrected-to-normal vision.

consented_count.value: Five subjects gave written informed consent

task_description.value: Subjects viewed multiple colored moving dots in which motion or color was relevant to the task during a given run while ignoring the other feature.

design_type.value: fully crossed factorial design; event-related trial design

instructions.value: For attend-motion trials, subjects were required to identify the direction of motion as quickly and accurately as possible. For attend-color trials, subjects were required to identify the predominant color as quickly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: Multiple colored moving dots within a central circular aperture of 7.5° diameter; motion coherence and color proportion varied independently.

task_description.value: Separate motion and color localizer tasks were used to generate regions of interest.

stimuli.value: Motion localizer: 10 s of 100% coherent dot motion followed by 30 s of static dots. Color localizer: 10 s of stationary colored squares followed by 30 s of grayscale squares.

description.value: Functional images consisted of 24 slices acquired with a gradient echoplanar imaging protocol. A projector displayed the image on a translucent screen inside the scanner bore; responses were collected with an MRI-safe fiber optic response pad.
Anatomical images consisted of 160 slices acquired using a T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid-acquisition gradient echo protocol.

fMRI preprocessing included conversion to 4D NIfTI, slice-timing correction, motion correction, 5 mm spatial smoothing, coregistration to structural images, and normalization to MNI_N27 standard volume.

steps.value: Functional images were converted to 4D NIfTI format.
Motion correction was performed using AFNI 3dvolreg, with the reference volume set to the mean image of the first run.
Images were smoothed with a 5 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.
Coregistration was performed using AFNI 3dAllineate with the local Pearson correlation cost function.
The anatomical image was warped to functional image space using the inverse transformation.
Anatomical images were normalized using FSL fnirt to MNI_N27.

hrf_model.value: γ probability density function peaking at 6 s

model_settings.value: Separate regressors modeled six levels of motion coherence, six levels of color coherence, and the attended/ignored feature. Linear trends used coherence vectors transformed to zero mean and normalized to a sum of squares equal to 1.

level.value: subject-level voxelwise fMRI statistical analyses, followed by group-level analyses

model_settings.value: The model fit reaction time and accuracy data using A′, k, and TR parameters; fits were optimized for log-likelihood (Lp) by an iterative procedure.

estimator.value: iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood (Lp) of the diffusion model fit

model_settings.value: A bottom-up input was modulated by a multiplicative top-down attentional factor for the duration of the reaction time; the best-fitting model was calculated via maximum likelihood.
Multivariate autoregressive models predicted upcoming time points; conditional Granger causality incorporated a third region into the model.
